en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Chapter The Fourteenth Chapter
The Discourse on the Unincluded:
Is the "state of views" (diṭṭhigata) unincluded? Yes.
Is the path, the fruit, and Nibbāna; the stream-entry path and the fruit of stream-entry; the once-return path and the fruit of once-returning;

the non-return path and the fruit of non-returning; the arahant path and the fruit of arahantship; and the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of power, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment [identical]?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that "a speculative view is not included"?
“Yes,” he said.
“Should it be said that an ordinary person (puthujjana) is ‘one who is free from lust for sensual pleasures’?
“Yes,” he said.
Should it be said that they are "free from views"?
One should not say so.
Therefore, it follows that the sphere of views (diṭṭhigata) is not included within the mundane (apariyāpanna).
The Discussion on the Unincluded is finished.
This is the fourteenth chapter. Its summary verse is as follows:
An unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root;
a wholesome root connects with an unwholesome root;
the six sense bases connect with the body of tactile consciousness.
Noble form is derived from the great elements;
that very underlying tendency is the obsession;
the obsession is dissociated from consciousness.
According to the element, that very thing underlies it:
a speculative view that is undeclared,
a speculative view that is unincluded.
